verdict: Ads went dark this week; the 28-day numbers still hold up.
narrative: Both Meta and Google have been at zero spend since September 17, meaning no leads have entered since September 16 — this is a structural pause, not a budget issue, and campaigns are being brought back online now. Over the full 28-day window you received 114 leads at $16.28 cost per lead, all sourced through Meta, which carried the period. Before the shutdown, efficiency was already softening — cost per lead rose 16% week-over-week and the daily lead rate had dropped sharply — so the restart will be paired with refreshed creative and tighter targeting. Google Ads ran $437.77 in spend over the 28 days with zero recorded conversions; that channel is being restructured before further budget flows through it. Expect campaigns back in market this week, with cleaner attribution as conversion tracking is brought current by end of September.
